technology.summary: Today's technology news includes the launch of Honor's Magic 9 Pro Max flagship phone in China, featuring a design revamp, a capable camera, and a large battery. Nvidia has announced a new AI safety platform to contain rogue agents within milliseconds, while Instinct, a viral AI agent, has raised $1 billion in Series C funding, valuing the company at $10 billion. In other news, maritime intelligence startup Quartermaster has raised $140 million, enabling real-time awareness for what it calls the "largest blind spot on Earth." Meanwhile, Microsoft has gone quiet after church groups asked for 1% of data center costs.

finance.summary:
Today's most important finance news includes the following:

- Chinese shares have touched a one-year low, led by a selloff in technology firms after a report that authorities may allow purchases of Nvidia Corp.’s new chips and proposed US sanctions on foreign optical producers.
- Small-cap stocks surged 23% in H1 FY27 as resilient earnings and strong liquidity fuel the rally, but stretched valuations and rising global risks leave little room for earnings disappointment.
- SS Retail shares surged nearly 7% on 28 September, gaining 83% since its IPO.
- Som Distilleries & Breweries shares rose nearly 7% after the Madhya Pradesh High Court quashed the state's rejection of its excise licence renewal application.
- Adani Enterprises shares dropped 3% after Adani group entities swapped 86 lakh shares for ₹2,498 crore.
- NSE share price today opened lower at ₹1,786 per share on the BSE and touched an intraday low of ₹1761 within a few minutes of the Opening Bell.
- Nalco share price emerged as the biggest laggard, as the stock fell as much as 3.89% to ₹344.65 per share. Meanwhile, Vedanta and Hindalco shares fell over 3% during the intraday session.

politics.summary:
The Supreme Court has cancelled Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre's bail in the Thane doctors' assault case, stating that the medical fraternity cannot be attacked.

The Court has also given rival factions four weeks to file pleadings, and the ECI three months to decide the TMC symbol row. This is in response to a petition by Bengal's former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, who challenged the Election Commission's decision to freeze the party symbol.

In other news, the Centre has been given permission to manufacture patented life-saving medicines, and the government has stated that 99% of CBSE schools are ready for the new three-language policy.

Chirag Paswan has expressed shame at being part of the government, due to rising molestation cases in Bihar.
